newsitem.title: FRANCE: Egyptian tender keeps wheat market in suspense.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian tender keeps wheat market in suspense.

text.p: Egypt is keeping world grain markets in suspense over the size of a wheat purchase slated for the end of the week, grain exporters said on Thursday.
Egypt is due to tender on November 15 to buy 50,000 tonnes of French wheat and 100,000 tonnes of Argentine wheat for shipment in December.
It is also seeking to import 50,000 tonnes of Australian wheat for shipment in December, exporters said.
But some exporters speculate that Egypt may buy more wheat than it is tendering for as it did in previous tenders.
U.S. wheat futures rallied on Wednesday partly on talk Egypt by the weekend would be in for 250,000 to 300,000 tonnes of wheat and that the business may go to the United States.
European grain exporters, however, said that much hinged on Egypt's appreciation of where world prices were heading.
Some traders argued that firmer wheat prices may force Egypt to limit the size of its wheat purchase.
"I think they will only seek to cover their needs for December. It is very unlikely that they will buy more than 150,000 tonnes," one trader said.
But other traders said that if Egypt believes that the fall in world prices is now over, it will seek to buy as much wheat as it can and seek cover until at least end January.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said on Wednesday that he expected world wheat prices to rebound as supplies became tighter.

Exporters also said that another element to take into account was the level of EU wheat subsidies this week as there are signs that the EU may scale down its wheat export subsidies due to budgetary problems.
